scan.source: OFFLINE DEMO — simulated external evidence — ZIP upload

limitations: This report is a point-in-time snapshot of the saved inventory and fresh OSV queries, not a live deployment assessment.
Dependency presence and advisory version matches do not prove runtime execution, attacker control, or actual exploitability.
No known advisory match is not a safety guarantee. Unknown, failed, paginated, or skipped checks are not clean findings.
Advisory IDs can be aliases of the same underlying issue; counts describe package instances, not distinct exploitable vulnerabilities.

Details are fetched for at most 40 unique advisory IDs; at most 100 matched package instances and 20 advisory IDs per finding are included. Descriptions, references, paths and source evidence are bounded.
Source-provided CVSS vectors are retained without inventing numeric scores or priorities. Withdrawn or mismatched records require manual review.

A verified candidate is an advisory-listed fixed release that exists in its ecosystem registry and returns no known OSV match at verification time. It is not a guarantee of safety, compatibility, or that every relevant fix was published.
At most three candidate releases per package/version are checked, for at most 20 unique pairs. If no candidate is verified, manual review is required. Major-version changes may require migration.
Transitive updates require changes to the owning dependency declaration or parent. No dependency graph or lockfile is changed automatically.

Only server-recorded scoped reachability results from this server process are included (latest result per instance, at most 100 instances per scan and 100 recent scans; not restored after restart). Their affected-export mappings are user-declared; NOT REACHABLE applies only within each declared coverage and is never a global safety claim.
No source code, submitted package scripts, or package installation is executed while preparing these reports. Testing and release-note review remain the maintainer's responsibility.
title: Security Findings

findings.whatIsWrong: OSV returned 1 advisory ID(s) for lodash@4.17.20 at this recorded dependency location.
findings.whyItMatters: The recorded dependency includes a version associated with published security advisories. Dependent packages or project roots may inherit this dependency impact. The advisory preconditions and application exposure must be evaluated separately.

report.reason: A syntactic call path reaches the user-declared affected export of the selected locked package instance.

coverage.boundary: Captured application source → declared export of the selected locked npm package instance.

limitations: Syntactic, context-insensitive ESM traversal of captured JS/JSX/TS/TSX/MJS/CJS source; no code is executed.
Entrypoints are user-declared. Module initialization and an optional named/default exported function are roots. Other externally invoked exports are outside coverage.
Target mapping is user-declared and not verified against an advisory. A target denotes an exported API boundary, not an internal library function.

External package initialization and internal code, node_modules, generated/missing source, native code, framework dispatch, callbacks, dynamic imports, CommonJS, reflection, and computed calls are not modeled.
Branches are conservatively traversed without feasibility analysis. REACHABLE means a syntactic call path, not proven runtime execution or exploitability.
NOT REACHABLE applies only to declared entrypoints, captured source, and the exported-boundary model. It is not evidence of application safety.
Source capture: 200 files, 256 KiB/file, 2 MiB total. Traversal: 1,000 units, 5,000 calls, 100,000 AST visits; evidence limited to 100 records.

results.name: lodash
reviewSteps: In a trusted development environment, use npm audit signatures to verify supported registry signatures and provenance. This report has not performed that verification.

metadata.description: SIMULATED registry metadata for offline demonstration

limitations: Heuristics are review signals, not proof of malicious intent. NO SIGNALS is not a safety guarantee. Metadata can be publisher-controlled.

Name similarity uses a fixed reference list v1 (react, react-dom, express, lodash, axios, typescript, webpack, vite, eslint, prettier, chalk, commander, mongoose, next, jquery, dotenv), one edit or adjacent transposition, minimum length five; scoped names are excluded. It does not cover all typosquatting or dependency confusion.
At most 100 unique exact package/version pairs and 1,000 instances are included, with a 15-second metadata deadline and 1 MiB response limit. Unavailable or omitted data is not clean.

Integrity compares recorded lock and registry digest strings only. Tarballs, installed bytes, signatures and provenance attestations are not downloaded or cryptographically verified. Matching metadata does not establish safety.
Provenance is registry-advertised evidence only. Missing provenance or signatures does not imply malware. Lifecycle scripts are common in legitimate packages and are never executed.

CONFIRMED MALICIOUS requires a fresh OSV version match and a verified, non-withdrawn MAL- advisory for the same npm package. This is an attributed source verdict, not an independent analysis; other advisory IDs and heuristics cannot confirm malware. Advisory detail coverage limits also apply.
